svg.aria-label: How to write 热: 10 strokes · 9 pen lifts · 10 movements
svg.title: Writing 热
svg.desc: 10 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of 热 (chinese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansSC-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after Hanzi Writer Data 热.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/%E7%83%AD.json>. Source note on variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 热, in three pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the hand piece as 打 opens: a horizontal, a vertical that hooks to the left at its foot without lifting, then a stroke rising to the right across it. Medians 4–6 draw the upper right: a left-falling stroke, a horizontal that turns down, bends right and hooks up without lifting, then a dot inside. Medians 7–10 draw the four dots along the foot as 点 ends. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hooks and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.
